title: buyers-cohort-procurement-thresholds-and-fallback-pathways-research
creator: Maya Chen
description: Research and produce a buyer-cohort driven map that correlates enterprise procurement thresholds (price, latency, contract length, SLAs) with practical fallback pathways and vendor switchability risk. Output will inform: 1) which model families we prioritize for pre-provisioning / Dedicated offers, 2) econometric thresholds for sales playbooks, and 3) a set of deterministic trigger rules for the Watchtower signal pipeline to start model-fallback or pre-warming workflows.
acceptance_criteria: A cohort taxonomy covering at least 5 enterprise buyer archetypes (e.g., FinServ-Compliance, High-Throughput-SaaS, Regulated-Health, Startups-PLG, Global-Platform)
For each cohort provide numeric procurement thresholds: acceptable P95 latency, per-10k-token cost sensitivity, minimum contract term, acceptable data residency constraints
A ranked fallback-pathways matrix that pairs primary model variants with two fallback options and estimated quality/regression delta for each pairing
A prototype switchability score (0-100) per vendor/model with documented signal inputs and an example Watchtower rule definition
Final artifacts: cohort CSV, fallback matrix CSV, a one-page executive brief, and a recommended set of 4 engineering tickets for integration into Watchtower and onboarding flows
tasks: Interview 6 account execs to capture recent procurement failure and switch examples
Run 12 procurement RFP post-mortems (sourced from deals in Salesforce) to extract thresholds
Quantitative analysis: join cost/latency data from console metrics with purchase outcomes
Benchmark regression delta for 8 candidate fallback pairs using evaluation prompt sets
Draft Watchtower trigger rule prototypes and validate with infra on feasibility
Write executive brief and workshop with Sales, Solutions, and Engineering
success_metrics: Scorecard: model-switchability scores computed for top 10 vendor+variant combos
Reduction in unexpected fallbacks in pilot accounts by >= 30% within 90 days after integration
Sales enablement: two procurement playbooks adopted by field teams
Watchtower rules: 3 automated triggers implemented in staging
risks: Data availability: console token-level cost attribution incomplete for older deals
Evaluation noise: regression delta estimates vary by prompt set and require guardrails
Org alignment: Sales may disagree with recommended contract term bands
Engineering bandwidth: Watchtower integration competes with runtime perf work
